non_blocking_notes: Defensive tamper signals (CREDENTIAL_TAMPER, SERVICE_TAMPER) added only to detection indicator set _STRONG_INDICATORS; no execution capability or recovery authority granted
Case-sensitive signal matching is enforced (lowercase variants return None), meeting exact matching requirement
Evidence-first failure behavior validated: audit failures raise RansomwareEvaluationDenied with EVIDENCE_WRITE_FAILED, maintaining failure safety
DRY_RUN and DETECT_ONLY modes preserved (signals only used for detection classification, no state mutation or response logic)
Test coverage includes distinct signal correlation (MEDIUM confidence, WARN recommendation), case sensitivity validation, and evidence failure semantics
result.reasoning_summary: Patch implements FW-RANSOM-05 defensive-control tamper signal correlation by adding CREDENTIAL_TAMPER and SERVICE_TAMPER tokens to the _STRONG_INDICATORS frozenset. Scope is appropriately narrow: two signals, two comprehensive tests, documentation updates only. Deterministic confidence: signals are immutable (frozenset), case matching is exact (test validates lowercase rejection), and correlation logic is pure. Evidence-first failure semantics are correct—when audit callback fails, RansomwareEvaluationDenied(EVIDENCE_WRITE_FAILED) is raised rather than silently omitting findings. No process authority, service control, credential access, recovery mechanism, or response action is introduced. DRY_RUN/DETECT_ONLY modes remain operative. Tests validate: (1) multi-source distinct signals produce MEDIUM confidence with WARN recommendation, (2) case sensitivity (lowercase variants return None), (3) evidence failure propagates as exception. All 20 tests pass; git diff --check passed. Patch is deterministic, safe, and meets defensive-control requirement.
